chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yahya ibn Sallam, from Yusuf ibn Yaqub, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yunus al-Shaybani, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'How is the humouring of some of you unto the others?' I said, 'Little'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not be doing so (being of little humour), for the humour is from the good morals, and you would be entering the cheerfulness by it upon your brother, and it was so that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would humour the man intending to cheer him up'.

key_terms.حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ: Good morals, excellent character, or good conduct
key_terms.مُدَاعَبَة: Humouring, playful interaction, or jesting in a friendly manner

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on humour and playful interaction among believers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while excessive or trivial playfulness is discouraged, genuine *mudababah* (affectionate banter) is a virtue of good character (*husn al-khuluq*) that fosters social cohesion. This tradition highlights the Prophetic model of using humor not for mockery, but as a deliberate act of kindness to alleviate the burdens of others, a concept deeply valued in Shia ethical teachings for maintaining brotherhood (*ukhuwwah*).
